The note pins measurement as 'the assignment of a quantity to a property' — an act. A sample rate is not that act: it is the parameter the act yields, a number (44100 Hz) characterizing a sampling configuration. A parameter is not a kind of the act that produces it; the instance of measurement would be the measuring, not the measured quantity. Law 9a — a thing is not an instance of its own property; the pinned sense fails. STRIKE.

A signal chain is, by its own accepted carve, a conceptual model representing an audio signal's route as an ordered sequence of processing stages. It is a representation of the route, not the processing activity. The processing is what the stages do to the signal; the chain is the ordering described. Law 9a: a thing is not an instance of its own property, and a model of an activity is not a kind of that activity. The pinned sense ('a specific kind of audio processing') fails against the target's carve. This is a previously rejected leap re-filed. STRIKE.

The target pins frequency as the number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit time. Sampling is a repeating event: each sample is one occurrence, and the sample rate counts those occurrences per second, expressed in hertz (44100 Hz is a frequency). A competent audio engineer calls the sample rate a frequency — the frequency of the sampling event. No nearer kind exists in the record (no bare 'rate' entry; only compounds like bit-rate), so frequency is the nearest kind. The pinned sense holds. ADVANCE.

A signal chain satisfies all three: the stages are ordered, each stage's audio output feeds the next (material flow), and the chain has a defined input and final output. The note pins the sense correctly: the ARRANGEMENT of stages, not the operations inside them — which is precisely the sense in which the audio-processing target failed and this one holds. No nearer accepted kind exists for 'ordered sequence of processing stages'; pipeline is it. A competent engineer calls a signal chain 'a pipeline.' ADVANCE.
